layout.arrangement: Entire slide content is enclosed by a thin red rectangular border. Title centered at top inside the border. Below the title, two side-by-side regions: LEFT (~9%-36% width) has a handwritten-style header 'e.g. Sobel 2-D filter' above a Grumpy Cat meme photo overlaid with a large red 3x3 matrix; RIGHT (~43%-93% width) has three overlapping RGB-tinted copies of the same meme (red back/top-right, green middle, blue front/bottom-left), a red bold label '3-D Filter', and at the far right an isometric 3x3x3 numbered cube with a yellow 'Third D' depth-dimension arrow annotation at its lower-left. A black letterbox bar runs across the very bottom (video frame artifact).

layout.hierarchy: Title dominates (largest, bold, red). Next largest are the red matrix numerals on the cat image. Medium: handwritten header and '3-D Filter' label. Small: white meme captions and yellow 'Third D'. Smallest: black cube numerals. Red is the dominant accent color throughout.

visual_elements.description: Grumpy Cat meme photo: white/gray cat with dark brown-gray ears and face markings, frowning, lying on white bedding. White bold all-caps caption 'I LOVE MATH' at top and 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' at bottom (classic meme layout). Overlaid on the cat's face is a 3x3 matrix in large red numerals with oversized red square brackets: row1 -1 0 1, row2 -2 0 2, row3 -1 0 1.
visual_elements.position: left panel, below the handwritten header

visual_elements.description: RGB channel-stack diagram: three identical copies of the same Grumpy Cat meme image, each tinted a single channel color and offset diagonally to suggest stacked 2-D channels: RED copy at back/top-right (caption 'I LOVE MATH' clearly visible), GREEN copy in middle ('I LOVE MATH' visible), BLUE copy at front/bottom-left (captions 'I LOVE MATH' and 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' faintly visible through the tint). Conceptually represents the three color channels of a 2-D image to motivate a 3-D filter.

Isometric 3x3x3 cube (3-D filter volume): light gray/white faces subdivided into 3x3 grids of cells by thin black lines, with a small black numeral in each visible cell. Numerals are blurry; best guesses - top face rows: '2 3 5' / '2 3 5' / '2 3 5' [?]; left face rows: '9 7' / '5 3' / '1 6 8' [?]; right face rows: '1 3 9' / '7 3 9' / '3 1 5' / '1 8 2 4' [?] (last row partially cut/unclear). Right face slightly darker gray than top face for 3-D shading.
visual_elements.position: far right, below the '3-D Filter' label

visual_elements.description: Depth-dimension annotation: thin black double-headed dimension arrow running parallel to the cube's lower-left depth edge (pointing from upper-right to lower-left), with small extension ticks, labeled 'Third D' in small yellow text with black outline, indicating the third (depth/channel) dimension of the cube.
Thin red rectangular border (no fill) framing the entire slide content including the title.
Solid black horizontal bar across the very bottom of the frame (video letterboxing, not part of the slide design).

typography_notes: Title: bold sans-serif (Arial-like), red, ~32-36pt, centered, sentence case with question mark (grammar error 'looks' preserved verbatim). 'e.g. Sobel 2-D filter': casual handwritten/marker-style font (Comic Sans-like), black, ~24pt, lowercase 'e.g.'. Matrix numerals: very large red sans-serif (~36-40pt) with oversized brackets. '3-D Filter': bold red sans-serif ~20pt. Meme captions: bold white ALL-CAPS sans (Impact-like). Cube numerals: small black ~10pt. 'Third D': small yellow italic-style text with black outline. No numbered bullets anywhere; slide is image/diagram driven.

recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to white (#FFFFFF). 2. Draw a rectangle with no fill and a ~2pt red (#C00000) outline, inset ~6% from left/right and ~7% from top to ~91% height, framing all content. 3. Add a centered text box near the top (y ~12-20%) with the exact text 'What would a k-D filter looks like?' (keep the verbatim grammar), Arial Bold ~34pt, red #C00000. 4. Left panel: add text box at x ~9%, y ~39% with 'e.g. Sobel 2-D filter' in Comic Sans MS (or similar handwritten font), black, ~24pt. 5. Below it, insert the Grumpy Cat meme image (approx 4:3, width ~27% of slide); if the image lacks captions, add white bold ALL-CAPS Arial text 'I LOVE MATH' at its top and 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' at its bottom. 6. Overlay the matrix on the image: create a 3x3 text grid with rows '-1 0 1', '-2 0 2', '-1 0 1' in red #C00000 bold ~36pt, and add two large red '[' and ']' bracket characters (scaled to ~120pt) flanking the grid, centered over the cat's face. 7. Center-right: paste three copies of the same meme image, each ~22% slide width, offset diagonally (~15% horizontal, ~12% vertical steps); recolor/tint the back copy red (#B00000), middle copy green (#00A000), front copy blue (#1414C8), ordering front-to-back as blue, green, red. 8. Add text box '3-D Filter' in red #C00000 bold ~20pt at x ~82%, y ~43%. 9. Far right: draw an isometric cube (PowerPoint 'Cube' shape, or three rhombi) filled light gray (#E8E8E8 top, #D0D0D0 sides) with thin black outlines; subdivide each visible face into a 3x3 grid with thin black lines and place small black numerals 1-9 in the cells (top face rows '2 3 5' x3, left face '9 7 / 5 3 / 1 6 8', right face '1 3 9 / 7 3 9 / 3 1 5' as best readable). 10. Add the depth annotation: draw a thin black double-headed arrow parallel to the cube's lower-left depth edge with small extension ticks, and place a small yellow (#FFFF00) text box with black outline reading 'Third D' beside it. 11. Optionally add a solid black rectangle across the full bottom ~5% of the slide to mimic the video letterbox bar.
